history: Dunhuang was the throat of the Silk Road — 'Dun means great; Huang means splendid'. The Mogao Grottoes hold 735 caves and 45,000 square meters of murals across a millennium — among China's first World Heritage sites in 1987. Crescent Lake has survived a thousand years beside the Singing Sand Dunes; Yumen and Yang Passes echo the frontier poetry of old.
importance: Pearl of the Silk Road · World treasury of Buddhist art
foods: Hand-pulled yellow noodles — called 'a wonder of China'.
Stewed lamb with thin pancakes soaked in gravy.
Sweet-sour drink brewed from Li Guang apricots.
Red-willow skewers of barbecue on the desert edge.
Fried glutinous rice puffs — hollow and crispy.
Thick chewy cold noodles, sour and spicy.
Wild desert onion scrambled with eggs.
Dunhuang sweet apricots — fresh or dried.
scenes: 735 caves and 45,000 square meters of murals — a treasury of Buddhist art.
The wonder of spring and dunes coexisting, never drying for a thousand years.
The Han-dynasty pass behind 'spring wind never crosses Yumen Pass'.
The old Silk Road of 'no old friends beyond Yang Pass'.
Wind-eroded yardang landforms like a demon castle.
Silk Road relics and Han-dynasty wooden slips.
A night market full of Silk Road flavor.
A famous Buddhist temple beside Crescent Lake.
